newsitem.title: FINLAND: SOCCER-MISSION IMPOSSIBLE AS FINNS FALL TO SWISS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MISSION IMPOSSIBLE AS FINNS FALL TO SWISS.

text.p: The closeness of the score belied
Switzerland's dominance as they comfortably beat Finland 3-2 in
a World Cup qualifying match on Sunday with the home side out of
their depth against a fluent and stylish Swiss team.
The defeat -- clearly foreseen by Finnish television which
introduced its coverage of the match with the theme tune from
the film "Mission Impossible" -- leaves Finland bottom of group
three with no points after two matches.
The visitors started sharply and went one up in the 14th
minute, Grasshopper Zurich striker Massimo Lombardo lifting a
well-judged lob over the head of Finnish keeper Antti Niemi from
just inside the area.
Switzerland extended their lead in the 34th minute when
striker Ciriaco Sforza latched on to a perfectly weighted cross
from fellow forward Stephane Chapulsat and drilled a long, low
shot into the far corner.
Finland, missing prolific Ajax Amsterdam striker Jari
Litmanen through injury, pulled one back just before half time
after striker Jari Vanhala was brought down in the penalty area
and Antti Sumialo converted from the spot.
Swiss midfielder Murat Yakin soon restored the margin,
connecting with a long floated pass from the left wing and
chesting the ball past a stranded Niemi eight minutes into the
second half to put Switzerland 3-1 ahead.
Substitute Joonas Kolkka grabbed a second Finnish goal in
the 74th minute, but only a string of first-class saves from
their beleaguered keeper saved Finland from far heavier defeat.
